# Clearer audit results

## Problem statement

The audit skill's end-of-session report Conclusion section buries the readiness
verdict ("Ready for ship") at the end of a long sentence, making it easy for
operators to miss when scanning reports. The verdict needs to be visually
prominent so operators can instantly see whether the item is ready to ship or
not.

## Users

- **Operators** reviewing audit results need to see at a glance whether the
  audited item is ready to ship.
- **Producers** scanning a grid of panes need the verdict to be immediately
  visible in the Conclusion section.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the session status is `completed`, the Conclusion section's first line
   is `✅ Ready to ship` (green) on its own line, followed by the completion
   sentence: `This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}).`
2. When the session status is **not** `completed`, the Conclusion section's
   first line is `🚫 Not ready to ship` (red) on its own line, followed by the
   incomplete-session sentence.
3. The green and red colouring is applied via ANSI escape sequences so that
   terminals supporting colour display the text in the correct colour, while
   plain-text terminals degrade gracefully (no garbled output).
4. All existing end-of-session reports across all skills (audit, intake, plan,
   implement, ship, …) use the new Conclusion format.
5. All existing tests for `render_report.py` pass; new tests cover the
   green/red colour formatting in both completed and incomplete states.

## Impact

Operators can now see at a glance whether an audited item is ready to ship by
looking at the colour and position of the verdict in the audit's Conclusion
section.

## Constraints

- The report renderer must work in plain-text (non-ANSI) terminals — colour
  is best-effort.
- The change must be backward-compatible with existing report consumers that
  parse the Conclusion section.
- The `next_action` parameter should no longer be appended at the end of the
  completion sentence (it is replaced by the standalone "Ready to ship" /
  "Not ready to ship" line).

## Existing state

The `render_report()` function in
`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` builds the Conclusion section as:

```
## Conclusion

This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}). Ready for {next_action}.
```

For incomplete sessions:

```
## Conclusion

{skill_name} session for {id} ({title}) is incomplete. Requires attention ({next_action}).
```

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — Modify the `render_report()`
  function's Conclusion section to move the readiness verdict to the top,
  in green or red.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — Update existing tests and add
  new tests for the colour-coded Conclusion format.

## Related work

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via
  helper report skill (the skill that introduced the report template).
- SA-0MQ01FDQ5003H09A – Implementation: update AMPA audit handlers to use wl audit-set (completed)
- SA-0MRCQ5K50007G3BB – Add ready-to-close audit gate to ship skill release process (completed)
- SA-0MQ01F8OJ007HEEP – Test: AMPA audit handler writes to audit_results via wl audit-set (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What format should the "not ready" message use? — Answer: "Not ready to ship" with red colour, mirroring the "Ready to ship" green format. Source: work item description ("or its negative counterpart").
- Q: Should the `next_action` parameter still appear in the Conclusion? — Answer: No — it is replaced by the standalone verdict line. Source: work item description says to "move" the readiness line to appear first.
data.title: Clearer audit results

## Problem statement

The tracked `.pi-config/agent/models.json` MunitoAI provider lists only `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`. The MunitoAI API serves two DeepSeek models, and the operator wants the newer `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` also available.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.pi-config/agent/models.json` exposes both paid MunitoAI DeepSeek models under one `MunitoAI` provider — `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` (existing) and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` (new) — with `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"`; no credential is committed.
- [ ] Both models share the same limits: `contextWindow: 400000`, `maxTokens: 16384`, `input: ["text"]`, `api: "openai-completions"`.
- [ ] The unverified limits for the new model are flagged as unverified (see note below).
- [ ] Tracked JSON formatting and indentation are preserved.

## Note on "flagged as unverified"

JSON has no comment syntax, so the "code comment" flag cannot live inside `models.json`. The flag is recorded in `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` (docstring/constant above the MunitoAI refresh) and in `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`. This resolution is an assumption; if the operator insists on an in-file marker, a non-standard `//` comment would make the file invalid JSON and is rejected.

## Key Files

- `.pi-config/agent/models.json` — add one entry to the MunitoAI models array

## Constraints

- Pure data change — no code or tests.
data.title: Update tracked models.json to add DeepSeek v4.1-flash-1017 to MunitoAI provider

# Regression test: phase_drive holds child lock for session lifetime

## Goal

Write a test that drives `phase_drive` with an injectable fake spawner and
asserts, from inside the spawner, that the per-child lock is held.

## Test location

Add to `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` (a new test class,
e.g. `TestDriveHoldsChildLockForSessionLifetime`) or extend
`test_drive_child_lock.py`.

## Assertions

Inside the fake spawner (called by phase_drive):

    def _fake_spawner(child_id, worktree_path, timeout, env):
        # 1. Kernel flock is live: an independent contender is refused.
        probe = _make_lock(worklog_dir, agent="intruder", session="probe")
        assert probe.acquire().acquired is False

        # 2. Lock file's recorded pid is a live process (the driver).
        metadata = json.loads(lock_file_path(child_id, worklog_dir).read_text())
        assert _pid_alive(metadata["pid"])
        assert metadata["pid"] == os.getpid()  # the driver process

        # 3. Token present in child env and matches the lock file.
        assert env[ENV_LOCK_TOKEN] == metadata["token"]

        return {"success": True, "returncode": 0, "reason": ""}

After phase_drive returns:

    # 4. Lock is released: a fresh acquire succeeds.
    assert _make_lock(worklog_dir, agent="next", session="next").acquire().acquired

Also assert a second child gets a fresh token (no stale-token reuse across
children).

## Existing suites that must stay green

- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_child_lock.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_lock.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 (covers parent AC5): Regression test with a fake spawner. A test drives
  `phase_drive` with an injectable fake spawner and asserts, from inside the
  spawner, that the lock is held (kernel `flock` live, recorded `pid` live,
  token present in the child environment) for the session's lifetime and
  released once the spawner returns.
- AC2: The test fails against the pre-fix code (no lock held during spawn).
- AC3 (covers parent AC5): The existing per-child-lock suites
  (`test_phase_start_child_lock.py`, `test_drive_child_lock.py`,
  `test_drive_child_session.py`) stay green.
- AC4 (covers parent AC7): Full project test suite passes with the new
  changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).
- AC5: The test does not use a fixed sleep; it asserts synchronously inside
  the spawner (which phase_drive holds while the lock is live).

## TDD ordering

This test slice comes FIRST (test-first), matching the parent lock epic's
Test -> Implement -> Docs structure. It pins the contract that
`SA-0MW7LMUUQ00701KJ` (the core fix) must satisfy; the implement child then
makes the assertions pass. If a red assertion cannot be committed green, mark
the new test `xfail`/`skip` so the suite stays green and have the implement
child remove the marker (never leave the tree red).

## Related

Parent: SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR
Precedes: SA-0MW7LMUUQ00701KJ (the core fix, which makes this test pass)

## Impact

A producer can stop worrying that a driven child silently drops back to `open`
mid-session: any change that stops the driver holding a child's lock while its
session runs now fails a named regression test with an actionable message.
data.title: Regression test: phase_drive holds child lock for session lifetime (fake spawner)

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py (13 doc-hygiene failures from commit ea3959b16, SA-0MVYDCUWA001Z8K0)
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
13 pre-existing failures on local dev base ea3959b16 (unpushed commit of SA-0MVYDCUWA001Z8K0), unrelated to any current slice:
1) tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py - 11 failures: _STEP_HEADING = "6.1. Parent recursion" no longer matches the relocated doc heading "### Relocated: Step 6.1 - Parent recursion (epic/parent items only)" in docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md.
2) tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py::TestEveryWorkItemSkillWired::test_final_step_section_requires_pasting_report_into_response - case mismatch: the test wants lowercase "paste it verbatim into"; skill/implement/SKILL.md now has capital "Paste it verbatim into".
3) tests/test_test_skill_wiring.py::test_all_wired_files_reference_test_skill - skill/implement/SKILL.md no longer contains the "skill/test" or "/skill:test" marker after the SKILL.md rewrite (it now links ../test/SKILL.md and uses $(skill_path test)/scripts/run_tests.py).
Fix surface: skill/implement/SKILL.md + docs/dev/implement-skill-re
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k 'tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py (13 doc-hygiene failures from commit ea3959b16, SA-0MVYDCUWA001Z8K0)'` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py (13 doc-hygiene failures from commit ea3959b16, SA-0MVYDCUWA001Z8K0)` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)
